page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7B12 processor provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The instance is allocated 64 GB of RAM, resulting in an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included, and no dedicated GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with this configuration.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU execution, ranking in the top tier for stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core performance, overall PassMark CPU scores, and Geekbench benchmarks remain in the middle tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 507.84 GB/s for cached reads and 69.61 GB/s for uncached reads. Performance drops occur in certain multi-threaded decompression tests like bzip3 and PassMark extended instruction sets, where results fall in the lower percentile. Application-level metrics show typical throughput, including 7.66 million SET operations per second on Redis and 7.24 GB/s for static web serving.

The e2-highmem-8 provides high memory density relative to vCPU count, offering cost efficiency for memory-bound applications that do not demand maximum parallel CPU compute throughput. The lack of attached local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage solutions. This profile makes the instance suitable for in-memory caching layers, database workloads, data processing pipelines, and web servers requiring significant memory overhead without heavy multi-threaded compute demands.
